# Revenue Bench

> Specialized recruitment for the revenue engine. Revenue Bench finds, assesses, places, and coaches sales talent that performs: sellers, sales leaders, enablement, and RevOps. Not just resumes that interview well.

Revenue Bench is a founder-led sales recruitment firm launched in 2026 by Carlos Garrido and Steve Swanston. Placements for selling and sales-leadership roles are assessed with the Objective Management Group (OMG) sales-specific assessment, and every placement arrives with a training refresher, gets a dedicated onboarding coach for the first 90 days, and is backed by a 90-day replacement guarantee. The firm serves high-growth and private-equity-backed companies, and maintains a pre-vetted "bench" of revenue talent so clients can hire without building their own pipeline.

Founder track record (stated separately, never combined): Carlos Garrido, an investment banker and growth advisor for more than 30 years, has supported $3B+ in client revenue growth and $6B+ in client exits. Steve Swanston has built revenue teams inside companies that exited for more than $500 million, and is Founder of Swanston Growth Advisors, a Certified Partner of Objective Management Group; Revenue Bench itself holds no such listing. Revenue Bench is a sister firm to Performance Edge, Swanston Growth Advisors, and Best Sales Team Training.

## Core pages

- [Home](https://revenuebench.io/): What Revenue Bench does, and why operators, not recruiters, find revenue.
- [Sales and Sales Leadership Recruitment for Employers](https://revenuebench.io/for-employers): The employer page: OMG assessment for selling and sales-leadership candidates, training on arrival, the 90-day onboarding coach, the published guarantee terms, and employer FAQs on search timing, fee structure, and what happens if the hire does not work out.
- [How It Works](https://revenuebench.io/how-it-works): The six-step search with a stage-by-stage timeline (typical durations, owners, and the standard cleared before each stage advances). Define the role, source from the bench, assess with OMG, present a true shortlist, place and train, then coach for 90 days. Kickoff to shortlist is commonly 2 to 4 weeks when the bench covers the role.
- [Hire a Revenue Leader for a PE-Backed Portfolio Company](https://revenuebench.io/private-equity): Recruiting and ramping the sellers and sales leaders a value-creation plan assumes, across a portfolio.
- [Sales Recruiters in Miami: What the Local B2B Sales Pool Holds](https://revenuebench.io/sales-recruiters-miami): The Miami-Fort Lauderdale-West Palm Beach sales-occupation table from the BLS May 2025 release (news release 26-1152-ATL, published 7 July 2026), read for a B2B employer. Sales and related occupations are 10.8% of local employment against 8.6% nationally, a location quotient of 1.25, but the occupations closest to complex-cycle B2B selling sit at or below the national concentration: sales engineers at 0.54 (510 employed) and technical and scientific product representatives at 0.92 (4,730 employed), while real estate agents run at 2.61 and travel agents at 4.56. Nine occupations with employment, concentration and mean annual wage, each with Revenue Bench's read of what it changes in a search; the adjacent-pool conversion framework (financial services, insurance, real estate, transactional reps) with what transfers, what does not, and what to test; the limits of the data, including that BLS annual wages are the hourly mean times 2,080 hours and exclude the self-employed; and when a local recruiter matters for a sales hire and when it does not. Revenue Bench's office is at 15601 SW 82nd Avenue, Palmetto Bay, FL 33157, (786) 547-9610, in Miami-Dade County and not in the City of Miami; the firm recruits nationally across the United States and is based in South Florida rather than limited to it. The interpretation columns are Revenue Bench's own read and carry no statistic.
- [Track Record: Every Result, Its Period and Who Delivered It](https://revenuebench.io/track-record): The attribution ledger, which sets every result and credential Revenue Bench publishes against the period it covers, the firm that delivered it, what it establishes for a Revenue Bench search and what it does not establish. $12M in net-new revenue over nine months after rebuilding a nine-rep sales team at a manufacturer, 200% growth in net-new sales over three months for a two-seller furniture brand, and 120% then 119% top-line growth across two consecutive years for a three-seller enterprise software team were all delivered through Performance Edge, Carlos Garrido's sales-effectiveness practice, before Revenue Bench was founded, and none is a Revenue Bench placement. Carlos Garrido's $3B+ in client revenue and $6B+ in client exits and Steve Swanston's record building revenue teams inside companies that exited for more than $500 million are separate records and are never combined. Objective Management Group's figures (72% reached the top half of their sales force, 9% against 33% first-year turnover, predictive validity in the 95 percent range, from OMG's 2024 validation survey on a dataset of nearly 2.4 million assessed salespeople as of 2023) are that group's own published data rather than independent peer-reviewed research, and the outcome comparisons set candidates the assessment recommended against candidates it advised against, so they describe selection rather than a measured effect on a hire. The Certified Partner listing belongs to Swanston Growth Advisors and Revenue Bench holds none of its own. Revenue Bench does not publish a placement count on this site and gives a written count by role type on request; the firm opened in June 2026, so no placement has been in role for twelve months, and a client introduction and the placement's start date are offered during an evaluation. The bench of pre-vetted sellers and sales leaders is listed with its own limit: no bench number is published, and a written, dated summary of how many fit a specific role is given on request. Also carries the published 90-day replacement guarantee terms and the limits of the record.
- [Sources: Every Statistic on This Site, With Its Sample, Period and Limits](https://revenuebench.io/sources): The provenance index. Twenty-five sources sit behind the external figures published on revenuebench.io, each with the party that produced it, the sample and period where the source publishes them, the figures drawn from it, and what it cannot be used to say. Independent research and government statistics (DePaul University's Center for Sales Leadership 2011-2012 Sales Effectiveness Survey, n=435 B2B sales organizations, 2011 data; Dow Scott and Thomas D. McMullen in WorldatWork Journal 26(3) Fall 2017, n=120, administered by Korn Ferry Hay Group in April 2017; Nick Toman, Bryan Kurey and Dave Lingebach in Harvard Business Review, October 2024, paywalled beyond two figures; US Bureau of Labor Statistics release 26-1152-ATL of 7 July 2026 covering May 2025; Bain, McKinsey and Goldman Sachs 2026 private markets research; CSO Insights and SBI Growth, both published with no sample size and no collection period, and listed as such; Paycor employer guidance of October 2025). Surveys and filings from inside the staffing and search industry (Top Echelon's 2019 survey of its own recruiting-network members; Staffing Industry Analysts' North America Staffing Company Survey 2021; Korn Ferry and Heidrick and Struggles annual reports; Clockwork Recruiting's Executive Search Performance Benchmark Report of October 2018, n=23,970 retained search projects run January 2015 to August 2018 in Clockwork's own customer base of search firms using its applicant tracking system rather than a random industry sample). Objective Management Group's own data, produced by the group that sells the assessment it describes and not independent peer-reviewed research (the 2024 validation survey, for which no sample size is published; predictive validity in the 95 percent range, which is the accuracy metric and never the top-half figure; the dataset of nearly 2.4 million assessed salespeople as of 2023 and the 6/11/33/50 distribution; 44,493 sales managers; the coaching study, n=11,078; the before-and-after training study, n=5,331; Sales DNA and competency prevalence; single-seller concentration, n=318; motivation; role fit; and hiring-manager intuition, which is research circulated in OMG's partner network by the firm Big Swift Kick rather than an OMG published study). Revenue Bench's own quantified working figures, which carry no external source and are labeled as estimates ($200,000 to $250,000 for a revenue-role mis-hire; 15% to 25% of new revenue as total sales cost). Also records the six figures Revenue Bench traced and left unpublished because no trail resolved to a source publishing a sample and a period: a counteroffer retention percentage, a bad-hire cost stated as a share of first-year salary, a one-year placement-success rate, an executive-hire failure rate, a contingency search success rate, and a search-performance figure presented as covering the whole category. Revenue Bench's own engagement results and the founders' records are on the track record page instead.
- [For Candidates](https://revenuebench.io/for-candidates): How revenue professionals get on the bench, assessed objectively, placed into system-led teams, and coached through their first 90 days. No cost to candidates.
- [About](https://revenuebench.io/about): The founders and the operator network behind every search.
- [Contact](https://revenuebench.io/contact): Tell us about the role you are filling, or that you want on the bench. A founder replies within one business day.

## Insights and guides

- [Why Sales Hires Fail: What 2.4 Million Assessments Show](https://revenuebench.io/guides/why-sales-hires-fail): Original analysis by co-founder Steve Swanston through Swanston Growth Advisors, a Certified Partner of Objective Management Group. Five failure patterns across what OMG describes as the largest sales-specific dataset in existence, the numbers behind each, and how to hire against them.
- [Should You Promote Your Best Rep Into Sales Management?](https://revenuebench.io/guides/should-you-promote-your-best-rep): Original analysis by Steve Swanston: in OMG's evaluation of 44,493 sales managers only 9% are strong in all three coaching qualities, selling and coaching are different measurable skills, and the four-move decision including the dual-track alternative.
- [The Private Equity Operating Partner's Sales-Hiring Playbook](https://revenuebench.io/guides/private-equity-sales-hiring-playbook): The four-phase governance model for sales talent across the hold (diligence, first 100 days, the build, exit preparation), the turnover math a portfolio multiplies (9% vs 33% first-year turnover in OMG's 2024 validation survey), and the standards to demand from any search partner.
- [How to Replace a VP of Sales Confidentially](https://revenuebench.io/guides/confidential-vp-of-sales-replacement): Confirming the replacement decision on assessment evidence, a six-stage confidentiality protocol (the risk, who is read in, and the control at each stage), the eight routes that expose a confidential search (board or investor update, HR systems and the requisition, LinkedIn adjacency, early reference calls, candidate back-channels, network overlap with the incumbent, interview logistics, and the circle expanding informally) with the early signal and containment move for each, what to do once a search is exposed, and the counteroffer fork on both sides (the incumbent resigning mid-search, and a finalist counteroffered by their current employer). Notes that no public study we could find measures how often a confidential search is exposed inside the hiring company, and that the widely repeated 80% counteroffer figure has no primary source. Cites OMG's 2024 validation survey (9% vs 33% first-year turnover, 72% reached the top half of their sales force).
- [Sales Recruiter Fees: Contingency, Retained, and What You Pay For](https://revenuebench.io/guides/sales-recruiter-fees): The three fee models (contingency, retained, container/engaged) compared by who carries the search risk, exclusivity, and the incentive each creates. Why the headline percentage is the wrong number to shop, since a wrong hire costs far more (DePaul's 2011-2012 Sales Effectiveness Survey: ~$115,000 fully loaded; Revenue Bench working figure $200,000 to $250,000), and how a 90-day replacement guarantee and an OMG assessment change the economics. Cites OMG's 2024 validation survey (72% reached the top half of their sales force, 9% vs 33% turnover).
- [Sales Team Due Diligence for Private Equity Buyers](https://revenuebench.io/guides/sales-team-due-diligence): The pre-LOI sales-team checklist a deal team can run from the data room, public sources, and management meetings before exclusivity, with the red flag for each area. What a sales-specific assessment of the leader and the quota-carrying team adds in the confirmatory window between the LOI and close, and the distribution to expect (OMG: 6% Elite, 11% Strong, 33% Serviceable, 50% Weak). The turnover cost math that re-prices the model (9% vs 33% first-year turnover in OMG's 2024 validation survey; DePaul's 2011-2012 Sales Effectiveness Survey: ~$49,508 average, ~$115,000 fully loaded), and the three outcomes: price it, plan for it, or pass.
- [The First 100 Days: Rebuilding a Portfolio Company's Sales Team](https://revenuebench.io/guides/first-100-days-portfolio-sales-team): The post-close decision sequence for an operating partner and a portfolio company CEO, published as a six-window table: the decision that closes in each window, the evidence it rests on, who owns it, and what running it late costs. Why the sales leader decision closes inside 30 days before any seat change below it, what a team baseline answers that a performance history cannot (OMG: 6% Elite, 11% Strong, 33% Serviceable, 50% Weak), why organization design closes before a search opens, and the written terms the first replacements run under. Cites OMG's evaluation of 44,493 sales managers (9% strong in all three coaching qualities, 80% more elite salespeople) and OMG's 2024 validation survey (9% vs 33% first-year turnover, 72% reached the top half of their sales force), with DePaul's 2011-2012 Sales Effectiveness Survey turnover costs (~$49,508 average, ~$115,000 fully loaded) and CSO Insights on ramp time.
- [How to Evaluate a Sales Recruitment Agency for the Role You Are Filling](https://revenuebench.io/guides/how-to-evaluate-a-sales-recruitment-agency): Revenue Bench's scored eight-criterion process scorecard names the document that proves every answer. Revenue Bench scores each process row 2 when the firm shows the document, 1 for a right answer with nothing in writing, and 0 for a vague answer, for a total out of 16; its comparison grid scores two or three firms side by side and its two disqualifying answers apply whatever a firm totals. The guide includes Revenue Bench's non-answer follow-up for every process row. Revenue Bench's separate four-question fit test, scored out of 8, asks for the firm's record at the role band, with the buyer and vertical, in the market where the candidate pool sits, and under the proposed search mechanism; the two Revenue Bench instruments are read separately and never added. Revenue Bench's five role bands are SDR and BDR; Account executive, mid-market; Enterprise seller and sales engineer; Sales manager; and VP of Sales and CRO. Top Echelon's 2019 survey of its recruiting-network members reports that a 90-day guarantee was most common at 44.9%, replacement with no money back was 61.4%, and a full refund was 8.4%. Staffing Industry Analysts' North America Staffing Company Survey 2021 reports that 20% of salary was the most common direct-hire fee. Korn Ferry's annual report for the fiscal year ended April 2025 and Heidrick and Struggles' annual report for the year ended December 2024 describe approximately one third of estimated first-year compensation plus a percentage for engagement expenses as the executive-search structure. Clockwork Recruiting's October 2018 report covers 23,970 anonymized retained search projects run January 2015 to August 2018 in Clockwork's own customer base of search firms using its applicant tracking system rather than a random industry sample; Clockwork reports a 60% placement rate at the least senior band against 78% for C-level searches and supplies no exact sales-specific figure. Revenue Bench answers its own eight process criteria and four fit questions, and Revenue Bench states that its June 2026 founding prevents it from supplying a twelve-month placement record.
- [Sales Recruiting Placement Guarantee Terms, Compared](https://revenuebench.io/guides/placement-guarantees-explained): The seven terms that decide whether a placement guarantee covers anything, compared in one table: window length, when the window starts, the remedy, the re-run count, the void conditions, who decides, and what support runs inside the window. Market figures come from Top Echelon's 2019 survey of its recruiting-network members (90 days 44.9%, 30 days 20.3%, 60 days 20.0%, six months 2.4%, one year 2.3%; replacement 61.4%, prorated refund 17.6%, full refund 8.4%), set beside Revenue Bench's own published terms: 90 days from the hire's start date, one free re-run, no conditions, the client's call, with a 90-day onboarding coach. Also works through whether a 12-month window beats a clean 90-day one, and includes a six-stage walkthrough of what using the guarantee involves.
- [When a Sales Hire Is Not Working Out: Cut, Coach, or Replace](https://revenuebench.io/guides/sales-hire-not-working-out): Triage for a struggling hire: wrong profile vs no process vs no onboarding, the check for each, the documented cost of waiting, and the recovery path.
- [The True Cost of a Bad Sales Hire](https://revenuebench.io/guides/cost-of-a-bad-sales-hire): The $200,000 to $250,000 working figure for a revenue-role mis-hire, plus the vacancy ledger, arithmetic that prices an open sales territory from the company's own quota, pipeline, ramp, and team inputs.
- [The 6% Problem](https://revenuebench.io/guides/the-6-percent-problem): Across what OMG describes as the largest sales-specific dataset in existence, only 6% are elite and half are weak.
- [Sales Assessment vs Interview: What Each Screen Catches](https://revenuebench.io/guides/sales-assessment-vs-interview): The division of labor in sales hiring: what the OMG screen measures (predictive validity in the 95 percent range, OMG's figure), what interviews alone can verify, and a decision table routing each hiring question to the screen built to decide it. Includes OMG's 2024 outcome figures, era-labeled, and the sequence Revenue Bench runs.
- [Will to Sell: Why Drive Is a Hiring Decision](https://revenuebench.io/guides/will-to-sell): OMG's construct explained for hiring teams: the five markers (Desire, Commitment, Motivation, Responsibility, Outlook), the before-and-after training study of 5,331 salespeople showing Will to Sell moved 0% to 6% while tactical skills jumped (OMG's data, labeled), and the five-marker table with what weak looks like in the first 90 days. Drive is screened before the hire; skill is coached after it.
- [How to Assess Sales Candidates Before Hiring](https://revenuebench.io/guides/how-to-assess-a-salesperson): The four traits that predict performance and the trait-evidence matrix: the evidence that counts for each trait, the false positive interviews accept, and the screen that measures it, with a credited selling-altitude check and OMG's labeled research figures.
- [The Sales Leader Interview Scorecard](https://revenuebench.io/guides/sales-leader-interview-scorecard): The pre-hire scoring instrument for VP of Sales, Head of Sales, and CRO interviews: seven weighted dimensions with anchored 1-to-5 answer patterns (coaching evidence and team building weighted heaviest), an independent-scoring protocol with advancement thresholds, and two disqualifiers that end a candidacy regardless of the total. The dimensions, weights, and thresholds are Revenue Bench's own instrument, labeled as such; the interview scores what only interviews decide, with drive and Sales DNA measured by assessment beforehand.
- [The Account Executive Interview Scorecard](https://revenuebench.io/guides/account-executive-interview-scorecard): The companion instrument for individual-contributor seller hires: seven weighted dimensions with anchored 1-to-5 answer patterns (verifiable track record and prospecting discipline weighted heaviest), an independent-scoring protocol with a worked weighted-total example, two disqualifiers, a printable score sheet with evidence fields, and defensibility guidance for using a cut-score instrument. The dimensions, weights, and thresholds are Revenue Bench's own instrument, labeled as such.
- [Reference Check Questions for Sales Candidates: What to Ask](https://revenuebench.io/guides/reference-checks-for-sales-hires): The consent-run protocol for the final screen: a five-step consent sequence with the current manager off the list by default, ten questions across verification, performance context, working reality, and the closing questions, each with what a weak answer sounds like, and the boundaries: many employers confirm only title and dates, a policy-limited answer is recorded as unavailable rather than negative, and references cannot decide future performance in a different role. The question set is Revenue Bench's own protocol, labeled as such.
- [Hiring RevOps and Sales Enablement: Scope and Sequence](https://revenuebench.io/guides/hiring-revenue-operations-and-enablement): The scope-and-sequence guide for the roles around a sales team. An eight-row scope table states who owns pipeline data, CRM, territories, process documentation, onboarding, skills training, content, and tooling before a dedicated hire exists, the observable condition that says the work needs an owner, and the failure pattern when it lands on the wrong desk. The maturity sequence is credited to Carlos Garrido's Developing a Scalable Sales Team framework from his Building a Scalable Sales Team masterclass. The page publishes no statistics by design; the sales-specific OMG assessment applies to selling and sales leadership roles, and operations or enablement candidates are selected on role-appropriate evidence instead.
- [The Founder's First Sales Hires: #1 Through #3](https://revenuebench.io/guides/founders-first-sales-hires): The hiring-sequence map for founder-led companies: what must exist before hires #1, #2, and #3, what each hire owns, what the founder's job becomes at each step, and the failure pattern each hire meets when its precondition is skipped. Hire #1 tests transferability, hire #2 proves the process travels, hire #3 marks the team threshold. Built on the who-runs-the-system progression from Carlos Garrido's Building a Scalable Sales Team masterclass; the map is Revenue Bench's own framework, labeled as such.
- [CRO, VP of Sales, or Fractional: Choosing the Sales Leadership Model](https://revenuebench.io/guides/choosing-a-sales-leadership-model): The stage-to-model matrix: five company stages defined by observable operating conditions (who closes, whether the motion repeats, how many functions share revenue responsibility), the model that fits each, what that leader must own, when each model breaks, and the trigger to change model. Includes the failure patterns (the CRO hired too early, the VP hired too late, the fractional engagement treated as permanent) and the honest option most guides skip: no full-time hire yet. The matrix is Revenue Bench's own framework, labeled as such.
- [How to Hire a VP of Sales or Sales Manager](https://revenuebench.io/guides/how-to-hire-a-vp-of-sales): The four mandates a VP of Sales can be hired to carry, builder, scaler, fixer, or successor, with the condition that calls for each, the evidence that confirms it in selection, the first 90 days, and the mis-hire signature at month six. Plus the three things to settle before the search opens, the four red flags, the 30/60/90-day scorecard, and the reference protocol. The four-mandate model is Revenue Bench's own framework with no statistic attached, and it follows the leadership-model decision rather than replacing it.
- [The 30-60-90 Day Plan for a New Sales Leader, as a Scorecard](https://revenuebench.io/guides/sales-leader-30-60-90-scorecard): The employer-side measurement instrument for a new VP of Sales or sales manager's first 90 days: fifteen milestones in three windows (learn the business by day 30, install the system by day 60, own the outcomes by day 90), each with what met looks like, the evidence to ask for, and what a miss signals, scored Met, Partial, or Missed at three gate reviews agreed before day one, with recovery actions at day 30 and the company's misses separated from the leader's. Includes a printable score sheet. The milestones and protocol are Revenue Bench's own instrument, labeled as such; the rhythm framing is credited to Carlos Garrido's Building a Scalable Sales Team masterclass, and coaching-frequency figures are OMG's study data (n=11,078), labeled.
- [The 90-Day Sales Onboarding Plan: Ramp a New Hire to Quota](https://revenuebench.io/guides/90-day-sales-onboarding-plan): The rep-side ramp instrument: five ramp gates (end of week 2 market contact through day-90 real quota), each with an exit condition, the evidence that counts, what a miss points to, and the correction that works at that point, with the hire's misses separated from the company's. The two-week market-contact standard and the reinforcement rituals are credited to Carlos Garrido's Building a Scalable Sales Team masterclass. Coaching figures are OMG's own research (weekly cadence, n=11,078); the 10-plus-month full-productivity figure is CSO Insights, third-party.
- [Building a Sales Talent Bench](https://revenuebench.io/guides/building-a-sales-talent-bench): The bench coverage map, Revenue Bench's own instrument: four exposures that open sales seats (planned growth seats, predictable attrition, key-person concentration, leadership succession), the signal each is live, what bench-ready coverage means, the upkeep, and the check that it holds up, plus the test of a working bench (assessed before need, recent contact, matched to the selling environment). The when-hiring-becomes-a-system progression is credited to Carlos Garrido's Developing a Scalable Sales Team framework. OMG's single-seller concentration figure (30% of sales teams, n=318) is OMG's own data, labeled; the DePaul figures (2011-2012 Sales Effectiveness Survey) and CSO Insights figures are third-party.
- [Sales Compensation Benchmarks for 2026](https://revenuebench.io/guides/sales-compensation-benchmarks-2026): How to set sales pay from two anchors, the market rate for the role and affordability (Revenue Bench's working range: 15% to 25% of new revenue as total sales cost), with a worked plan ledger labeled as illustration, a no-dollar role-design table, and the three sources a market number comes from. Publishes no salary table by design; the motivation figure cited is OMG's research.
- [Sales Recruiter vs Hiring In-House: How to Choose](https://revenuebench.io/guides/sales-recruiter-vs-in-house): The build-or-buy conditions table, Revenue Bench's own instrument: five conditions an in-house sales search needs (volume and repetition, a sales-specific screen, a live bench, the selling-environment match, a structured landing), the signal you have each, what its absence costs, and the check before you decide, plus the honest build list for companies that keep the search in-house. The selling-environment match publishes the five dimensions that decide whether a sales history transfers (buyer altitude, average order size, sell-cycle length, competition intensity, price position), from the interview battery Carlos Garrido teaches in his Building a Scalable Sales Team masterclass. The mis-hire figure of $200,000 to $250,000 is Revenue Bench's own working estimate; DePaul Center for Sales Leadership's turnover figures (2011-2012 Sales Effectiveness Survey) are third-party; OMG figures are OMG's own data, labeled; the hiring-manager intuition figure is partner-network research, not an OMG published study.
- [Sales-Leader Compensation in a PE-Backed Company](https://revenuebench.io/guides/pe-sales-leader-compensation): How a sponsor-backed package is built, component by component, and why equity, ramp protection, and exit terms behave differently under a sponsor.
- [The Sales-Hiring Mistakes PE Deal Teams Repeat](https://revenuebench.io/guides/pe-sales-hiring-mistakes): The capstone of the private-equity series. Eight sales-hiring mistakes deal teams repeat, set out in a repeated-mistake ledger that pairs each mistake with the belief it rests on, the event where its cost surfaces, and the evidence check that closes it. Two things here appear nowhere else on the site: the timing model, which says when a mistake made at diligence reaches the numbers, and a printable sales-risk block for the investment committee memo, eight assertion lines with the evidence each one requires. OMG figures are Objective Management Group's data, labeled, applied through co-founder Steve Swanston's OMG Certified Partner firm, Swanston Growth Advisors; cost figures are DePaul Center for Sales Leadership's 2011-2012 Sales Effectiveness Survey, on the cost of sales turnover. The ledger is Revenue Bench's own pattern observation, labeled as such, and the operating thesis is credited to Carlos Garrido's Building a Scalable Sales Team masterclass.
- [The Sales Leader You Inherited: Keep, Coach, or Replace](https://revenuebench.io/guides/inherited-sales-leader-keep-coach-replace): The decision a new owner or a private equity operating partner closes in days 16 to 30 after a deal, resolved as a six-gate decision tree with an explicit route out of every gate: whose numbers the leader is being judged on (four questions that separate the leader's contribution from results produced under a previous owner, a different compensation plan, and a pipeline built to be presented), whether the person manages or still carries the number personally, which of the three coaching qualities an evaluation finds missing, whether that gap is an untaught method or a want gap (the two doors), whether an agreed coaching cadence still runs thirty days later, and what keep with defined support says in writing. Includes the written support test with its review date and decision routes, the rollover-equity and earnout complication, and the cost of getting it wrong in each direction. OMG figures are Objective Management Group's data, labeled, applied through co-founder Steve Swanston's OMG Certified Partner firm, Swanston Growth Advisors; the before-and-after training study measured salespeople rather than sales managers and is labeled as such; chief revenue officer transition figures are Harvard Business Review's, October 2024; cost figures are DePaul Center for Sales Leadership's 2011-2012 Sales Effectiveness Survey. The gate sequence and the support test are Revenue Bench's own instruments, and the two-door framing, the stage model, and the coaching-versus-conversation distinction are credited to Carlos Garrido's sales-leadership teaching.
- [Your VP of Sales Resigned: Should You Counteroffer?](https://revenuebench.io/guides/vp-of-sales-resigned-counteroffer): The employer-side counteroffer decision, for a chief executive, founder, or private equity operating partner whose sales leader has just resigned and no replacement decision had been made. Treats a counteroffer as a hiring decision priced at a premium and applies the standard the replacement search would use. Two instruments: a seven-question decision table (would you hire this person today at the new number; were they pulled or pushed; is the reason they gave the reason; did they run a search or did a search find them; what changes on Monday if they stay; what the new number does to the pay band; who owns the forecast, the largest accounts, and the team's confidence for the next two quarters) with what points each way and the evidence that settles it, and a three-instrument comparison of the counteroffer, the retention agreement, and the accepted resignation with a managed transition, priced by what each buys, costs, signals, and how it ends. Also the window argument: a resignation is often known to almost nobody at the moment it lands, which gives the company a period to prepare a search before the team or the market knows a vacancy may exist, and a counteroffer spends that period. States that the widely repeated counteroffer retention figure has no primary source and links the trail published on the confidential-replacement guide. Counteroffer practice figures are from Dow Scott and Thomas D. McMullen, WorldatWork Journal, Fall 2017, a survey of 120 rewards and human resources professionals administered by Korn Ferry Hay Group in April 2017, labeled as self-reported organizational practice rather than measured retention outcomes; chief revenue officer transition figures are Harvard Business Review's, October 2024, framed as what follows a change. The decision table and the instrument comparison are Revenue Bench's own instruments, and the resignation-conversation question is credited to Carlos Garrido's Building a Scalable Sales Team masterclass alongside two of his 11 Golden Rules of Sales Leadership.
- [All Insights](https://revenuebench.io/guides): The full library, thirty-one field guides routed by the decision in front of the buyer: choosing how to run the search, deciding who to hire, hiring or replacing a sales leader, building the shape of the team, hiring inside a deal or a portfolio company, and fixing a hire that is already in place. Every guide carries a working artifact, a scorecard, a protocol, a checklist, or a table, and the router names which artifact each one hands you.
